title: Predicting cellular responses to perturbation across diverse contexts with State.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Hugging Face (HF) API listings: arcinstitute/State-Replogle-Filtered is one 30.0 GB h5ad (single-cell file) plus split .toml files (opened k562_zeroshot.toml: whole cell line held out as test). arcinstitute/PIE_tahoe100m: 50 per-cell-line DE (differential expression) parquets totalling 23.5 GB (~470 MB each), plus preprocessed matrices (fold_changes.npy 4.13 GB, fdr.npy 4.13 GB, tested.npy 1.03 GB). Opened meta.json: 56,827 rows (cell line x drug-dose), 18,151 genes, 50 cell lines (Cellosaurus IDs), 1,137 drug-dose conditions named by compound name + dose. Fetched the last 2 MB of one parquet: valid PAR1 footer. SE-600M weights are public (not gated), under a non-commercial licence. GitHub repo ArcInstitute/state is public. tahoebio/Tahoe-100M is CC0 and not gated.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: No full text (paywalled, no PMCID); only the abstract. Column meanings, cell counts per line (95.6M cells total) and DE method (Mann-Whitney U vs DMSO controls) come from the PIE_tahoe100m README, not from opening the parquet rows or the .npy matrices. I did not open any fold-change values, so missingness and value ranges are unchecked. ST-Tahoe model repo returned 401 (likely gated or renamed).

a1_downloadable.note: HF datasets State-Replogle-Filtered, PIE_tahoe100m and Tahoe-100M (CC0) list files publicly without login; checked via the HF API. The Virtual Cell Challenge dataset returned 401 (unauthorized).

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Label = per-gene log2 fold change of drug-treated vs DMSO (solvent control) cells, already computed per (cell line, drug-dose, gene) in the PIE DE parquets and as a dense matrix fold_changes.npy. Seen in the README and meta.json shapes, not in the values.

a3_inputs_present.note: Inputs are a cell-line ID (Cellosaurus, 50) and a drug-dose string (1,137). Drug structure (SMILES, the text encoding of a molecule) needs a lookup for ~379 compounds; Tahoe-100M ships drug metadata, which I did not open. Small lookup, not thousands.

a4_units_stated.note: README states log2 fold change, CP10k (counts per 10,000) normalisation, dose in uM (micromolar) in the condition name. From the README only.

a5_enough_rows.note: 56,827 (cell line x drug-dose) response profiles over 18,151 genes, read from meta.json. Unit of independence is closer to 379 drugs x 50 cell lines.

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: ~0.5-1 GB after subsetting to ~2,000 genes; full fold_changes.npy is 4.13 GB
a6_fits_laptop.note: Full dense matrix is 4.13 GB float32 (memory-mappable). Subsetting to highly variable genes keeps it well under 16 GB RAM; the raw 30 GB h5ad and 23.5 GB parquets are not needed. Download of 4.1 GB is still required.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: meta.json 56,827 rows is consistent with 50 lines x 1,137 conditions minus the 23 missing pairs the README lists (1,133-1,136 per line). Could not compare with the State paper's own counts (no full text).

a8_label_provenance.note: Fold changes are computed from measured single-cell RNA counts (treated vs DMSO), not from another model. Not derived from the model inputs (cell-line ID, drug identity).

B1.why: One dense matrix fold_changes.npy (56,827 x 18,151) with row index files; seen in HF listing and meta.json.

B2.why: .npy and parquet formats, valid parquet footer checked; values not loaded, 4.1 GB download needed.

B3.why: One platform, one lab (Tahoe Mosaic), one DE pipeline against per-line DMSO controls, per README.

B4.why: Untested genes set to 0 with a tested.npy mask; needs masking policy, documented in README.

B5.why: One row per (cell line, drug-dose) by construction of the matrix; per meta.json vocabularies.

B6.why: README documents every parquet column and every .npy array shape and meaning.

C1.why: Held-out-cell-line transfer is informative, but mostly meaningful only if it beats strong baselines.

C2.why: State, PIE, Tahoe-x1, scGPT, CPA/chemCPA, GEARS, VCC winners; several open with honest held-out evaluation.

C3.why: Weak angle: re-test linear/DepMap-informed baselines against State on unseen cell lines; already actively studied.

C4.why: Measuring each drug x cell line response by single-cell sequencing is costly lab work.

C5.why: State's published numbers plus obvious dummies (per-drug mean across cell lines, zero change).

D1.why: SE-600M State embedding weights public on HF (checked, not gated); ChemBERTa/MolFormer for drugs.

D2.why: Embedding cells needs raw counts and SE-600M (715M parameters), slow on CPU; pseudobulk features avoid this.

D3.why: State model licence is non-commercial (read MODEL_LICENSE.md); Tahoe-100M data CC0.

E1.why: Hold out whole cell lines or whole drugs; State's own toml configs do zero-shot cell-line holds.

E2.why: 50 cell lines and ~379 drugs are enough groups to hold out.

E3.why: Per-drug mean across training cell lines and zero-change baseline are trivially computable.

E4.why: Three doses per drug and many cells per condition; replicate plates per README are not confirmed.

E5.why: Known effects: proteasome or HDAC inhibitors give large, shared signatures; dose-response monotonicity should be recovered.

E6.why: Shuffle cell-line labels, ablate drug features; straightforward on a matrix.

E7.why: LINCS L1000 drug signatures and sci-Plex give independent drug x cell line responses.

E8.why: No full text seen; cannot confirm which State number is reproducible on which split.

G1.why: Cellosaurus cell-line IDs and gene symbols in meta.json; drug names need mapping to InChIKey.

G2.why: DepMap expression/dependency (cell line) and LINCS L1000 (compound + cell line).

G3.why: Cellosaurus to DepMap is near one-to-one; drug name to InChIKey has salt-form ambiguity.

G4.why: Baseline omics predicting drug response is a known question; marginal over State's context features.

H1.why: Every drug-dose measured in every line, including non-responding genes and weak drugs.

H2.why: 50 cancer cell lines, one lab and platform; no primary tissue or normal cells besides hTERT-HPNE.

H3.why: Claim stated precisely below: cancer cell lines, one platform, 24h-style screen doses.

H4.why: Cell-line-only scope obvious; dose/time limits and plate effects only partly documented in README.

I1.why: Arc Institute virtual-cell team, Tahoe Therapeutics, Virtual Cell Challenge community.

I2.why: Marginal: a better unseen-line predictor would only shift screen design if gains are large.

I3.why: Correlation of fold changes vs. the real need (ranking drugs/hit genes per line) is roughly aligned.

I4.why: Published work shows linear/mean baselines are hard to beat here; ML gain uncertain.

J1.why: Real modelling: grouped splits, transfer to unseen cell lines, embeddings, calibrated metrics.

J2.why: Some intuition on drug classes; perturbation-metric pitfalls need expert check.

J3.why: A baseline-vs-State table on held-out lines is shareable at any stage.

existing_models.name: State (this paper; SE-600M embedding + ST transition model)
existing_models.score_and_split: Abstract: >30% better perturbation discrimination and better DE-gene recovery than baselines on large datasets; zero-shot cell-line holds per its toml configs. Exact numbers not seen (no full text).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Generalising to cellular contexts with no perturbations observed during training (abstract framing).

existing_models.name: PIE (Arc Institute perturbation effect model, ArcInstitute/pie)
existing_models.score_and_split: Not retrieved; HF card says Tahoe is a training set of its cross-dataset experiment.

existing_models.name: Linear baselines vs GEARS/scGPT/scFoundation/CPA (Ahlmann-Eltze et al., Nature Methods 2025)
existing_models.score_and_split: No deep model beat simple linear baselines on single/double genetic perturbations (Norman, Replogle).
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: Deep models do not yet beat linear baselines for unseen perturbations.

existing_models.name: Calibrated-metric re-evaluation (Nature Biotechnology 2026, 'Deep learning perturbation models can outperform baselines on calibrated metrics')
existing_models.score_and_split: Argues deep models beat uninformative baselines under calibrated metrics; numbers not retrieved.

existing_models.name: Virtual Cell Challenge 2025 winners (BioMap xTrimoSCPerturb, Altos flow matching, TransPert)
existing_models.score_and_split: Held-out H1 stem-cell CRISPRi perturbations (300 perturbations); hybrid statistical+DL models won.
existing_models.authors_named_unsolved: 2026 challenge targets cell contexts never seen in training.

backbone.name: SE-600M (State embedding model) for cell context; ChemBERTa or MolFormer for drug structure
backbone.hardware: Laptop CPU for pseudobulk/fold-change features plus molecule embeddings; SE-600M cell embedding over raw cells would want a GPU
backbone.licence: State: Arc non-commercial licence; Tahoe-100M data CC0

integration.partner_dataset: DepMap (baseline expression and gene dependency of the same cancer cell lines) and LINCS L1000
integration.join_key: Cellosaurus accession (to DepMap model ID); drug name to InChIKey
integration.bigger_question_one_sentence: Does a cell line's untreated expression and dependency profile predict how its transcriptome responds to a drug it was never screened with, as well as State does?

controls.positive_control: Recover strong shared signatures of proteasome/HDAC inhibitors and monotonic dose-response across the three doses.
controls.negative_control: Shuffle cell-line identities across rows and replace drug embeddings with noise; performance must fall to the per-drug mean.
controls.external_validation: LINCS L1000 or sci-Plex signatures for overlapping drug x cell line pairs.

honest_claim_h3: Predicts the pseudobulk gene-level fold change of a drug at one of three doses in a cancer cell line held out of training, among the 50 lines and ~379 compounds Tahoe chose to screen on one platform.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a cancer cell line's untreated profile plus a drug's structure to predict how the drug changes that line's gene activity.
plain_idea.train_on: Each example is one cell line x drug-dose pair, described by the line's baseline expression and the drug's chemical structure; 56,827 pairs (from meta.json).
plain_idea.predict: The change in activity of each of ~18,000 genes (log fold change vs solvent-treated cells), measured by single-cell RNA sequencing in the Tahoe-100M screen.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Drug-screen teams could skip screening some cell lines if simple baselines transfer; if they fail, it quantifies how much State adds over cheap features.

more_or_better_data.why: State itself was trained on this exact Tahoe-100M data plus Replogle and Parse PBMC (167M cells for embeddings); we would have strictly less.

confidence_score.why: Three doses and per-condition cell counts allow noise estimates, but I did not check whether State or PIE already report uncertainty.

models_beatable.why: State is a 2026 Cell model with open code evaluated on held-out cell lines; Virtual Cell Challenge drew 300+ final teams.

guaranteed_improvement.why: No new data joins that State did not already see; DepMap adds a different assay, so improvement is not guaranteed by construction.

label_elsewhere.sources: LINCS L1000 (known resource: compound x cell line expression signatures), sci-Plex (known resource), Tahoe-100M raw counts (checked on HF).
label_elsewhere.join_key: Cellosaurus ID / cell line name; InChIKey for drugs
label_elsewhere.why: Independent drug-response signatures allow testing whether a model trained on Tahoe transfers to another lab and assay.

ambitious.why: Publishes perturbation-model benchmarks; would need a clear result that cheap baselines match or beat State on unseen cell lines.

realistic.why: Fits a focused benchmark note comparing simple transfer baselines to State on held-out Tahoe cell lines.

fallback.journal: bioRxiv preprint plus a NeurIPS/ICML biology workshop
fallback.why: A negative or partial baseline comparison is still a useful workshop contribution in this active community.

pitch.headline: A ready matrix of 56,827 drug x cancer-cell-line responses over 18,151 genes, CC0 source data, no single-cell processing needed.
pitch.what_makes_the_data_unusual: Every one of 1,137 drug-dose conditions measured in each of 50 cell lines (95.6M cells, per README), so whole lines or drugs can be held out cleanly.
pitch.the_win: Show a DepMap-baseline linear model matches State's correlation on held-out cell lines (State's exact numbers not seen; paper paywalled).
pitch.even_if_it_fails: A measured gap between cheap baselines and State on held-out cell lines, which the field is actively disputing.
pitch.who_wants_it: Arc Institute virtual-cell team, Tahoe Therapeutics, and Virtual Cell Challenge entrants deciding whether large cell-embedding models are worth their cost.

ml_idea: Hold out whole cell lines in the PIE Tahoe fold-change matrix; compare per-drug mean, ridge regression on DepMap baseline expression + drug fingerprints, and State predictions on the top ~2,000 variable genes.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: memory-map 4.1 GB fold_changes.npy, slice ~2,000 genes, ridge on 56,827 rows; molecule embeddings for ~379 drugs take minutes.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Download fold_changes.npy + tested.npy and count how many (line, drug) rows have a non-trivial response (e.g. >50 genes FDR<0.05); if most are near zero, the task collapses to the mean.

verdict_reason: Data is clean and open (56,827 profiles, CC0 source) but the task is saturated: State was trained on this very data, with open code and held-out cell-line evaluation, alongside PIE, linear-baseline benchmarks and the Virtual Cell Challenge. Only a baseline re-evaluation remains, and the paywalled text prevents checking State's numbers.
